docs.text: Michigan environmental experts say that the state’s groundwater system is so expansive that it should be treated as a sixth Great Lake. The state’s groundwater network contains as much water as Lake Huron, and more than half of all Michigan residents and businesses rely on groundwater day to day.
This is why I won't move away from the Great Lakes. Need to be as near the only reliable source of fresh water in the future as possible.

Yes, I have a well, but water is six feet down in the Great Lakes, because primeval sea. I am more hesitant about wells in PNW. Also--so many people burning firewood. I may not be able to go outside a bubble. But still looking for a place with clean air. (There is a southernmost point of AU.)

Also, there are parts of the world that can handle the water stress, and space, of a course, like around the Great Lakes. Fuck them in the Colorado River watershed, though. The issues of pesticides and letting people turn the local ecosystem psychedelically weird is another issue, however…

We had to deal with well water up north at the cottages we rented in the summers on Lake Michigan when I was a kid, but I don't remember it being hard as hell. If drinking unfiltered water from springs becomes a regular thing for MAGAs, you'll be one of the people dealing with the aftermath.
